brief: AI credit spreads (hyperscaler complex) are at the year's widest. The last time spreads were this wide, the underlying equities were 15% lower. The debate has shifted from near-term earnings revisions to AI capex having peaked and questions over financing, sustainability and capital returns. Pessimism is rising, breadth is low, and put volume hit its second-highest level of the year. Goldman's non-AI call has worked, and with the NDX still at 21x earnings, AI multiples reflect uncertainty rather than overvaluation. Positioning shows beta-adjusted nets at the 67th percentile over five years versus net leverage at the 17th, with cyclicals-vs-defensives pricing only 2% growth, down from 6%. Since the market is absorbing stress through rotation rather than index-level declines, Goldman still favors the broadening trade: ex-AI equity upside via SPXXAI call spreads and a European basket, a Quality Comeback trade (up 20% over three months, though RSI above 80 flags reversal risk), a defensive Healthcare trade in ACA-exposed beneficiaries tied to midterm subsidy reauthorization odds, an uncorrelated Brazil re-rating trade into Oct 25, and Taiwan AI hedges after TSMC fell 2.3% despite raised guidance.
